## Compatible governance updates at task startup

Repositories can opt into a single update check at the start of a new top-level Codex task.
The parent assesses the work already underway. Minor changes remain eligible; substantial
implementation, review, and release certification retain their current runtime.

Compatible releases are verified and installed before an isolated local runtime-lock commit.
Unrelated staged and unstaged work is preserved. Ordinary hooks and signing stay enabled.
Subagents and task continuations never initiate updates. Major releases, migrations, and startup
integration changes require deliberate adoption.

Opt-in is a one-time repository change after deliberately adopting 2.5.0. Run
`project-governance startup enable --provider codex`, review and commit its integration changes,
trust the native hooks, and start a fresh task. No background service or scheduler is added.

Claude startup adoption remains disabled pending complete live parent/child proof. Gemini through
Antigravity remains manual because the current hook contract lacks native root-task identity.

Releases now include digest-bound `runtime-update.json` compatibility metadata alongside the wheel
and runtime lock. Missing metadata safely keeps older releases on deliberate adoption.
